newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ANDERSON DOUBLE HELPS MONACO CRUSH LE HAVRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANDERSON DOUBLE HELPS MONACO CRUSH LE HAVRE.

text.p: Brazilian Sonny Anderson struck twice as leaders Monaco crushed Le Havre 3-0 in the French first division on Friday and moved seven points clear of second-placed Paris St Germain.
Anderson opened the scoring in the eighth minute and Victor Ikpeba made it 2-0 with a diving header in the 29th minute.
Le Havre's hopes of salvaging something from the game disappeared 18 minutes into the second half when Anderson scored his second goal of the night and his 15th this season.
PSG had cut the gap between themselves and the leaders to four points after recording their first victory for nearly three months with a 2-1 win at Lens on Thursday.
The game was interrupted for 10 minutes after a linesman was knocked out by a missile thrown from a section of the stands occupied by Lens fans.
The incident will be the subject of an inquiry by French league officials and could lead to Lens being banned from playing one or several matches in their stadium.
Former European champions Marseille delighted their fans on Friday by thrashing Lille 5-1.
David Garcion put Lille ahead in the 26th minute but Marseille, who had lost to Lille in a French Cup first round tie last week, ran the visiting side ragged after the break.
Marc Libbra and Xavier Gravelaine each scored twice. Olivier Echouafni was their other marksman.
The matches between Caen and Bastia and Guingamp and Bordeaux were postponed because of flooded pitches.
